title: Ares Management Reportedly in Talks for Minority Stake in Kolkata Knight Riders
excerpt: Moneycontrol reporting says the US asset manager is in advanced discussions over about 20% of the IPL franchise from the Mehta Group, at a valuation of over $1.8 billion — with no final agreement reached.
body:
• US alternative asset manager Ares Management is reportedly in talks to acquire a minority stake in Kolkata Knight Riders, according to Moneycontrol reporting cited in fresh reports this week — no final agreement has been reached.
  • The Mehta Group, a co-owner of the franchise, is reportedly exploring the sale of about 20% of KKR in a transaction that would value the franchise at over $1.8 billion, according to the same reporting.
  • KKR is owned by Knight Riders Sports Private Ltd: Shah Rukh Khan's Red Chillies Entertainment holds 55% and the Mehta Group 45%, and investment bank Nomura has been mandated as sell-side advisor.
  • For fans, nothing has changed yet: the talks are reported, not signed, and KKR's ownership today remains exactly as it has been since 2008.

Ares Management, the US-based alternative asset manager, is in talks to buy a minority stake in Kolkata Knight Riders, according to reports. Moneycontrol, citing sources familiar with the matter, has reported that Ares is in advanced discussions over a minority holding in the three-time Indian Premier League champions, and Storyboard18 and other outlets have reported the underlying stake-sale process at the franchise. The reporting is explicit on one point: no final agreement has been reached, and the terms under discussion could still change.

What has been reported

According to the Moneycontrol report, summarised by Investing.com, the Mehta Group is exploring the sale of approximately 20% of KKR, with the franchise valued at over $1.8 billion in the potential transaction. Investment bank Nomura has been mandated as the sell-side advisor. Sources familiar with the negotiations told Moneycontrol that substantive discussions have taken place, but that no final decision has been made and any deal remains contingent on the structure and terms still being deliberated.

The stake-sale process itself is older than the Ares link. Moneycontrol first reported on December 18, 2025 that a minority sale was being evaluated at KKR, with only the Mehta Group considering a divestment to unlock value. At that stage the discussions were described as preliminary, with the size of the stake and the valuation still under evaluation, and the process was expected to formally kick off in early 2026. Ares was named as a prospective buyer in Moneycontrol's later reporting, and the talks have resurfaced in reports this week ahead of the IPL 2027 season.

"KKR is owned by Knight Riders Sports Private Ltd: Shah Rukh Khan's Red Chillies Entertainment holds 55% and the Mehta Group 45%, and investment bank Nomura has been mandated as sell-side advisor."

Who owns KKR today

KKR is owned by Knight Riders Sports Private Ltd, a joint venture formed in 2008 between Red Chillies Entertainment, promoted by actor Shah Rukh Khan, and the Mehta Group, backed by actress Juhi Chawla and industrialist Jay Mehta. Red Chillies is understood to hold a 55 percent stake, with the Mehta Group holding the remaining 45 percent. That split is unchanged, and any Ares transaction, if completed, would come out of the Mehta Group's holding rather than Khan's, according to the reporting.

The Knight Riders group has also built a global T20 footprint that matters to diaspora fans: it owns Trinbago Knight Riders in the Caribbean Premier League, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders in the UAE's ILT20, and Los Angeles Knight Riders in Major League Cricket in the United States. When KKR was approached during the earlier reporting on the stake sale, a franchise spokesperson declined to comment, and Red Chillies Entertainment, Jay Mehta, Juhi Chawla, the Mehta Group and Nomura did not respond to queries.

Why IPL franchises are drawing global investors

The reported talks fit a wider wave of dealmaking around IPL teams. Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals have both weighed larger ownership changes: Rajasthan Royals' promoters initiated discussions around a controlling stake sale at a valuation of over $1 billion, while United Spirits Ltd has been reviewing its investment in RCB, reportedly seeking a valuation of around $2 billion. Ares already holds sports investments including Chelsea FC in the English Premier League and the Miami Dolphins in the NFL, according to the Moneycontrol reporting.

The financial case investors cite starts with the league itself. Houlihan Lokey's IPL Valuation Study 2025 put the overall business value of the league at $18.5 billion and its brand value at $3.9 billion, with KKR's brand value estimated at $227 million, fourth among franchises. Long-term media rights, centralised revenue sharing and a salary cap give IPL teams comparatively predictable cash flows, which is what makes minority stakes in them legible to institutional buyers.

What happens next

What to watch is paperwork, not press coverage: a signed agreement, its stake size and price, and any regulatory or league approvals that follow. Until then, this remains what the sources say it is — talks. KKR, three-time champions after titles in 2012, 2014 and 2024 and based at Eden Gardens in Kolkata, go into the IPL 2027 cycle with the same owners they have had since the league began.
nri_angle: KKR's owner group also runs the Los Angeles Knight Riders in Major League Cricket, so a US institutional buyer for the IPL franchise would deepen the Knight Riders brand's American footprint.
author: Diaspora Desk
